result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.colorize_node_attrs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Map node attribute values to colors. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10269-L10426){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.colorize_node_attrs( node_attr_from=None, values=None, node_attr_to="color", palette="default", alpha=None, nodes=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Colorize node attributes](/assets/graphs/colorize-node-attrs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a six-node graph whose nodes carry a community attribute, shown as badges with the values 0, 1, and 2. After: each node has a color written from its value, so the two nodes with 0 are in the accent color, the two with 1 in teal, and the two with 2 in violet." width="100%"} Sets a color attribute on nodes based on categorical or continuous values. For categorical data, assigns distinct colors from a palette. For continuous data, interpolates between colors. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_attr_from]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Attribute name to read values from (e.g., 'community', 'type'). If `None`, must provide values dict. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, Any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Dictionary mapping node IDs to values. If `None`, reads from `node_attr_from=` attribute. [node_attr_to]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["color"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Attribute name to write colors to (e.g., 'color', 'fillcolor', etc.). [palette]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["default"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Color palette name or list of hex color strings. Available palettes: ColorBrewer (e.g., 'Greens', 'RdBu', 'Set1'), Viridis ('viridis', 'magma', 'plasma'), or 'default'. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Alpha transparency (0-100), not yet implemented. [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[list[str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Subset of nodes to colorize (default: all nodes). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Detecting communities first and then colorizing by that attribute gives each community a visually distinct color: ::: {#3fe5ba37 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec G = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(6): G.add_node(label=str(i)) # Create two communities G.add_edge(source="0", target="1") G.add_edge(source="1", target="2") G.add_edge(source="0", target="2") G.add_edge(source="3", target="4") G.add_edge(source="4", target="5") G.add_edge(source="3", target="5") G.cmty_louvain(attr_name="community") G.colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="community", palette="vibrant") G.get_node_attrs("color") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: '#e41a1c', 1: '#e41a1c', 5: '#377eb8', 6: '#377eb8', 4: '#377eb8', 2: '#e41a1c'} ``` ::: ::: Any categorical attribute works the same way, not just detected communities: ::: {#699ea4c0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} G = ec.Graph() G.add_node(label="A", type="person") G.add_node(label="B", type="person") G.add_node(label="C", type="organization") G.add_edge(source="A", target="B") G.add_edge(source="B", target="C") G.colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="type", palette="tableau") G.get_node_attrs("color") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {2: '#f28e2c', 3: '#4e79a7', 1: '#f28e2c'} ``` ::: ::: A plain list of hex colors can be passed instead of a named palette, assigned in the order values are encountered: ::: {#4740bab5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} G = ec.Graph() G.add_node(label="A", status="active") G.add_node(label="B", status="inactive") G.add_edge(source="A", target="B") G.colorize_node_attrs( node_attr_from="status", palette=["#ff0000", "#00ff00"] ) G.get_node_attrs("color") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {2: '#00ff00', 1: '#ff0000'} ``` ::: :::
